title: Systems from Zero
tagline: Networks, operating systems, SQL and NoSQL databases, database internals, Kafka, Redis and big data, from first principles to labs on your laptop, one focused session a day.

envs.what: The lab box: a Linux shell with JDK 25, strace, tcpdump, ss, tc, dig and friends (`box-priv` for privileged steps).
A small network of lab boxes: two LANs, routers, a tunnel with a small MTU, a dual-stack IPv6 subnet, web servers.
PostgreSQL 18 with the course database `course` (`psql -U sfz -d course`), pageinspect and pg_stat_statements.
A PostgreSQL 18 primary with a streaming standby, a replication slot and a WAL archive; `--profile pitr` adds a point-in-time restore.
DynamoDB Local on localhost:8000: the real DynamoDB API, no AWS account.
Apache Cassandra 5.0, one node, with the payments keyspace.

Cassandra 5.0, three nodes, for the ring, gossip, quorums and repair. `--profile grow` adds a fourth node and `--profile dc2` a second datacenter (about 4 GB with both); stop it with `--profile grow --profile dc2 down -v`. About 3 minutes to start.
Cassandra 6.0 alpha with Accord transactions, for one optional Try-it.
MongoDB 9.0 as a one-member replica set.
MongoDB 9.0, three members, for failover and write concern.
A sharded MongoDB 9.0 cluster: a config server replica set, two shards and a `mongos` router.
Neo4j Community with the fraud graph, browser on localhost:7474.
OpenSearch, one node, for the search Try-its.
OpenSearch, three nodes, for shards, replicas and a node leaving. Uses port 9200, so stop `opensearch.yml` first.
TimescaleDB on PostgreSQL 18, for time-series.
PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector, for vector search.
Apache Kafka 4.4, one KRaft node on localhost:9092. Profiles add Schema Registry (`--profile schemas`) and Debezium CDC (`--profile cdc`).
Kafka 4.4, three nodes, for replication and the ISR.
Redis 8.10, one node (`exec redis redis-cli` for a prompt). `--profile small` adds a 4 MB server for eviction.
Redis primary, replica and three Sentinels, for replication and failover.
Redis Cluster with three primaries on ports 7001 to 7003.

tracks.title: Computer networking
tracks.short: Packets, addresses, routing, UDP and TCP, DNS, TLS and HTTP/3, seen with real tools on your laptop.

lessons.title: What happens when you curl a URL
The link layer: Ethernet, MAC addresses and ARP
IP addresses, subnets and NAT
Routing, ICMP and traceroute
IPv6 for application engineers
UDP and the sockets API
TCP connections: handshake, states and TIME_WAIT

DNS: how a name becomes an address
TLS 1.3, certificates and mTLS
HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 over QUIC
Production networking: load balancers, timeouts, retries and pools

tracks.title: Operating systems
tracks.short: System calls, processes and threads, scheduling, virtual memory, the page cache, I/O models and containers, traced on a real Linux box.

lessons.title: What a kernel does: system calls and user mode
Processes: fork, exec, wait and signals
Threads, and how the JVM maps them to the OS
CPU scheduling: EEVDF, nice and CPU quotas
Locks at the OS level: futexes and deadlock

Copy-on-write, mmap and the OOM killer
Memory allocation: malloc, arenas and why RSS grows

File systems: inodes, links and file descriptors
I/O models: blocking, epoll and io_uring
Containers are processes: namespaces and cgroups

tracks.title: Relational databases and SQL
tracks.short: The relational model, schema design, joins, window functions, recursive queries, indexes, EXPLAIN and isolation levels on PostgreSQL 18, and how to run a PostgreSQL server: configuration, roles, replication, backups and failover.

lessons.title: The relational model, keys and NULL
Designing a schema: normalization and constraints
Joins, including semi and anti joins
Aggregation: GROUP BY, FILTER, ROLLUP and GROUPING SETS
Subqueries and common table expressions
Recursive CTEs: trees and graphs in SQL
Window functions: ranking, LAG and running totals
Window frames and gaps-and-islands
LATERAL joins, top-N per group and keyset pagination
JSONB, upserts and MERGE
Indexes and reading EXPLAIN
Transactions and isolation levels
Row locks, SKIP LOCKED and job queues
SQL from the JVM: JDBC, pools, batching and migrations
Running PostgreSQL: processes, configuration, roles and connections
PostgreSQL replication, backups and failover

tracks.title: Database internals
tracks.short: Build the pieces of a storage engine yourself: a log-structured store, slotted pages, a buffer pool, a B+tree, an LSM tree, a WAL, MVCC, a query executor and Raft.

Column stores and compression
Replication and consensus with Raft

tracks.title: NoSQL databases
tracks.short: Key-value, document, wide-column, graph, search and vector stores, the distributed ideas under them, and then inside each store: Cassandra's ring and gossip, MongoDB sharding, DynamoDB's partitions, Neo4j and OpenSearch, and how to set each one up.

DynamoDB under the hood: partitions, routers and capacity
Inside Neo4j: native graph storage, memory and clustering
Inside a search cluster: OpenSearch nodes, shards and replicas

tracks.title: Kafka with Java and Kotlin

tracks.title: Redis with Java and Kotlin
